messages.subject: Plot title after layout change
parts:
I've been experimenting with customizing the layout of graphics after
plotting with ggplot. I want to stich two graphs together that are the
same height but different widths (1 is skinny...the other is wide).

I have avoided placing a plot title on each of the separate graphs
before stitching them together because this throws off the alignment
of the vertical axis if I just use one title on one graph...or it
looks funny if both graphs have to share the same title so they align
properly after stitching.

The code I am using to stitch together my two graphs (p4 & p5) (which
share the same ylim) is below. Can anyone recommend a good way to
apply a chart title to the resulting graphic so that both graphs share
one title?

Resulting Graph = [url]http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3734701/Example.jpg[/
url]

Layout = grid.layout(nrow=1,ncol=2,
widths=unit(c(2,8),
c("null","null")),
heights=unit(c(5),
c("null")))
grid.show.layout(Layout)
vplayout = function(...){
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=Layout))
}
subplot <- function(x, y) viewport(layout.pos.row=x,
layout.pos.col=y)
combplot <- function(a, b) {
vplayout()
print(a, vp=subplot(1,1))
print(b, vp=subplot(1,2))
}

p6 = combplot(p5, p4)

Thanks in advance for any help!

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Plot title after layout change
parts:
Hi,

I don't know if this is the best way for ggplot2, but you can directly
draw the title via grid.text as follows:

grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(nrow=2,ncol=2,widths=unit(c(2,8),c("null","null")),heights=unit(c(1,9),c("null")))))
subplot<-function(x, y)viewport(layout.pos.row=x,layout.pos.col=y)
print(qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars), vp=subplot(2,1))
print(qplot(mpg, wt, data=mtcars,colour=cyl), vp=subplot(2,2))
grid.text("TITLE OF THIS FIGURE", vp=subplot(1,1:2))

HTH.
